steps.title: Korean Pronouns Overview
steps.body: Korean has two registers for first-person pronouns: polite and casual. 저 (jeo) is the polite 'I', used with strangers, seniors, and in formal settings. 나 (na) is the casual 'I', used with close friends and younger people. Crucially, Korean very often drops the subject pronoun entirely when context is clear — 어디 가요? can mean 'Where are you going?' without any pronoun at all. Mastering when NOT to use a pronoun is as important as knowing the pronouns themselves.

tip.label: Pro-drop language
tip.text: Korean is a pro-drop language — when the subject is obvious from context or was mentioned recently, drop the pronoun. Leaving it in can sound unnatural or even slightly rude (overly direct). 저 괜찮아요 and 괜찮아요 both mean 'I'm fine', but the shorter form is more natural.

steps.body_ja: 韓国語の一人称代名詞には2つのレジスターがあります：丁寧形とカジュアル形。저（jeo）は丁寧な「私」で、初対面の人・目上の人・フォーマルな場面で使います。나（na）はカジュアルな「私」で、親しい友人や年下の人に使います。重要なのは、文脈が明らかな場合、韓国語では主語の代名詞をほぼ省略するという点です。어디 가요?は代名詞なしで「どこへ行くの?」を意味します。代名詞を使わないタイミングを知ることも、代名詞そのものを覚えるのと同じくらい大切です。

tip_ja.label: 代名詞省略言語
tip_ja.text: 韓国語は主語省略言語です——文脈から主語が明らかだったり最近言及された場合、代名詞は省略します。そのまま言うと不自然に聞こえたり、やや失礼に聞こえることもあります。저 괜찮아요と괜찮아요はどちらも「大丈夫です」ですが、短い形のほうが自然です。

steps.meaning: I (subject, polite) — 저 + subject marker 가 → 제가

steps.prompt: Which pronoun is the polite form of 'I'?

steps.title: Saying 'You' in Korean
steps.body: Korean avoids the direct pronoun 'you' (당신) in most everyday speech — it can sound cold, confrontational, or overly formal depending on context. Instead, Koreans use the person's name, title, or relationship term. A teacher would be called 선생님 (teacher), not 당신. A friend would be called by name. The pronoun 당신 appears in songs, poetry, and formal writing but is uncommon in daily conversation.

tip.label: How to address people without 당신
tip.text: Use the person's name + 씨 for adults you don't know well: 김민준씨. Use their job title: 사장님 (boss), 과장님 (manager). Use relationship terms: 언니, 오빠, 아저씨. These are far more natural than 당신.

steps.body_ja: 韓国語は日常会話で直接的な「あなた」（당신）をほぼ使いません。文脈によっては冷たく・対立的・または過度にフォーマルに聞こえるからです。代わりに、相手の名前・肩書き・関係を示す言葉を使います。先生は선생님（先生）と呼ぶのであって、당신とは言いません。友達は名前で呼びます。당신は歌・詩・フォーマルな文章には登場しますが、日常会話ではほとんど使われません。

tip_ja.label: 당신を使わずに呼びかける方法
tip_ja.text: あまり親しくない大人には名前 + 씨を使います：김민준씨。職業の肩書きを使います：사장님（社長・上司）、과장님（課長）。関係を示す語を使います：언니、오빠、아저씨。これらは당신よりはるかに自然です。

steps.meaning: I (topic, polite) — 저 + topic marker 는 → 저는

steps.prompt: Why do Koreans rarely say 당신 in conversation?
choices: It can sound cold or confrontational
steps.correct: It can sound cold or confrontational

steps.title: Third Person & We (그·그녀·우리)
steps.body: Korean rarely uses he/she pronouns in speech. Instead, Koreans say the person's name or use demonstratives: 그 사람 (that person), 이 사람 (this person). 그 (geu) and 그녀 (geunyeo) do exist — he/she — but they appear mostly in writing and translation. 우리 (uri) means 'we' or 'our'. Interestingly, Koreans use 우리 where English uses 'my': 우리 엄마 (my mom, literally 'our mom') — this reflects a collectivist cultural sense of shared family.

tip.label: 우리 = my (for family & country)
tip.text: 우리 나라 (our country), 우리 집 (my/our house), 우리 엄마 (my mom) — these are natural and common. Using 나의 나라 or 나의 집 instead sounds unnatural, almost cold.

steps.body_ja: 韓国語は会話で三人称代名詞をほとんど使いません。代わりに、相手の名前や指示語を使います：그 사람（その人）、이 사람（この人）。그（geu）と 그녀（geunyeo）という「彼/彼女」の代名詞は存在しますが、ほとんど文章や翻訳文で使われます。우리（uri）は「私たち」または「私たちの」を意味します。興味深いことに、韓国人は英語で「私の」と言う場面で 우리 を使います：우리 엄마（私のお母さん、直訳「私たちのお母さん」）——これは家族を共有するという集団主義的な文化を反映しています。

tip_ja.label: 우리 ＝ 私の（家族・国）
tip_ja.text: うり 나라（私たちの国）、우리 집（私の/私たちの家）、우리 엄마（私のお母さん）——これらは自然でよく使われます。代わりに 나의 나라 や 나의 집 を使うと不自然で、やや冷たく聞こえます。

steps.meaning: we / our (often used as 'my' for shared things)
steps.meaning_ja: 私たち / 私たちの（「私の」にも使う）

steps.meaning: we / our (humble, polite form of 우리)
that person (= he / she, informal way)
steps.meaning_ja: その人（非公式の三人称）
彼ら・彼女ら（書き言葉）

steps.prompt: 우리 엄마 literally means 'our mom' but is used to mean…
Which form of 'we' is more humble and polite, used toward seniors?

steps.title: Demonstrative Pronouns (이·그·저)
steps.body: Korean has three levels of demonstratives based on spatial distance. 이 (i) = near the speaker. 그 (geu) = near the listener or previously mentioned. 저 (jeo) = far from both speaker and listener. These attach to 것 (geot, 'thing') to form pronouns: 이것 (this), 그것 (that), 저것 (that over there). In casual speech these are shortened: 이거, 그거, 저거. The same 이/그/저 roots also work with place words: 여기 (here), 거기 (there), 저기 (over there).

tip.label: 이/그/저 vs 여기/거기/저기
tip.text: 이/그/저 + 것 = this/that thing. 이/그/저 + -(e)gi = here/there. So 여기 (yeo-gi) = here (near speaker), 거기 (geo-gi) = there (near listener), 저기 (jeo-gi) = over there (far from both).

steps.body_ja: 韓国語には空間的な距離に基づく3段階の指示語があります。이（i）＝話者の近く。그（geu）＝聞き手の近く、または以前に言及した物事。저（jeo）＝話者・聞き手両方から遠い。これらは 것（geot、「もの」）に付いて代名詞を形成します：이것（これ）、그것（それ）、저것（あれ）。カジュアルな会話では短縮されます：이거、그거、저거。同じ이/그/저は場所の語とも組み合わせられます：여기（ここ）、거기（そこ）、저기（あそこ）。

tip_ja.label: 이/그/저 vs 여기/거기/저기
tip_ja.text: 이/그/저 + 것 ＝ これ/それ/あれ（もの）。이/그/저 + -(e)gi ＝ ここ/そこ/あそこ（場所）。なので 여기（yeo-gi）＝ ここ（話者の近く）、거기（geo-gi）＝ そこ（聞き手の近く）、저기（jeo-gi）＝ あそこ（両者から遠い）。

steps.meaning: that (thing) — near listener or already mentioned
steps.meaning_ja: それ（聞き手の近くまたは既出）

steps.meaning: that thing over there — far from both

steps.prompt: Which demonstrative refers to something far from BOTH the speaker AND the listener?
저것 is the formal version. What is the casual version?

steps.title: Question Pronouns (의문대명사)
steps.body: Korean question words are placed in the same sentence position as the word they replace — unlike English, which moves 'what' and 'where' to the front. Compare: 영화 봐요? (You watch a movie?) vs 뭐 봐요? (What do you watch?). The question word simply swaps into the original slot. The main question pronouns are: 누구 (who), 무엇/뭐 (what), 어디 (where), 언제 (when), 왜 (why), 어떻게 (how), 얼마 (how much).

tip.label: No question inversion needed
tip.text: English moves the question word to the front and inverts subject-verb order: 'What are you doing?' Korean keeps the word order the same as a statement and just swaps in the question word: 뭐 해요? (What [are you] doing?) — literally 'what do?'

steps.body_ja: 韓国語の疑問語は、置き換える語と同じ文の位置に置きます。英語では「what」や「where」を文頭に移動させますが、韓国語は異なります。比較：영화 봐요?（映画を見ますか?）対 뭐 봐요?（何を見ますか?）。疑問語は元の位置にそのまま置き換えられます。主な疑問代名詞：누구（誰）、무엇/뭐（何）、어디（どこ）、언제（いつ）、왜（なぜ）、어떻게（どのように）、얼마（いくら）。

tip_ja.label: 疑問の倒置は不要
tip_ja.text: 英語では疑問語を文頭に移動し主語と動詞の順序を倒置させます：「What are you doing?」。韓国語では平叙文と同じ語順のまま疑問語を置き換えます：뭐 해요?（何していますか?）——文字通り「何する?」。

steps.meaning_ja: 何（カジュアル・よく使う）

steps.title: Pronouns Complete!
steps.message: You've mastered Korean pronouns — from polite 저 to casual 나, from 우리 (our/my), to demonstratives and question words. Great progress!
